brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: 4 hex-acc-keyhole hangers on the back face: accessory:0#0,0#2, 0#1,0#2, 0#2,0#2 on the bottom storey and 1#0,0#2, 1#2,0#2 on the top storey.
12 hex-acc-hook plates (24 hooks) on the front face, two per cell on both storeys.

requirements.requirement: Keyhole hangers on the back face and hooks on the front face, so tools hang away from the wall
requirements.evidence: The keyholes all sit on face slot 2 and the hooks on face slots 4 and 5, the opposite side of the row. I took the hook side to be the front; the configurator doesn't name which way faces the wall.

requirements.requirement: Holds small hand tools on its hooks
requirements.evidence: The hooks are there, but the configurator only hangs a cable coil, tape or goggles on a hook and refused pliers, so I showed gaffer tape and a cable coil instead. Nothing here can show a hand tool hanging or check how much weight a hook holds.

finish.summary: I built a three-cell, two-storey wall rack (51 parts). It has 4 keyhole hangers on the back face and 12 hook plates (two hooks each, 24 hooks) on the front face of every cell on both storeys. Open faces are capped and the joints are bolted; the build check found no errors and the mesh check is clear. Two gaffer tape rolls and a cable coil hang on the upper hooks to show it in use. The configurator only lets those props hang on hooks, so I couldn't show hand tools hanging. Nothing here can check how much weight the plastic hooks, hangers or wall screws hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
